newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia govt says no objection to Jackson show.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia govt says no objection to Jackson show.

text.p: The Malaysian government does not object to a planned concert by pop superstar Michael Jackson, although the show has been banned by one of the country's 13 states, a cabinet minister said on Wednesday.

"It is now up to the sponsors to find a suitable place like Kuala Lumpur for the show since the Selangor state had objected to the staging of the concert," Culture, Arts and Tourism Minister Sabbaruddin Chik was quoted by the national Bernama news agency as saying.
Sabbaruddin added that he had asked the cabinet for a ruling on the matter at its weekly meeting on Wednesday and was told it did not object to the show.
Jackson was scheduled to perform at the 80,000-capacity Shah Alam Stadium in central Selangor state next to the capital Kuala Lumpur on October 27.
But the state's municipal council revoked the booking last week, saying the pop star and his concert would have undesirable effects on Malaysia's youth.
A spokesman for the organisers said they were looking for a suitable venue.

"We don't have a place yet but we can't hold the show on any other day as it'll disrupt his (Jackson's) programme," said David Ling of DLG Communications Sdn Bhd, publicists for organisers Jojo Entertainment.
The stop in Kuala Lumpur is part of Jackson's world tour to promote his album, HIStory.
Last year, Selangor state cancelled a concert by rock star Rod Stewart at the same stadium, calling the show unpatriotic as it would have coincided with Malaysia's Independence Day on August 31.
